dataCheck.authzHint: A successful sign-in only means the credential is authenticated; whether a protected endpoint can be called still depends on the engine's authorization policy. When the credential is sent and the engine still answers 403, the cell is marked "authenticated but not authorized" and shows the engine's reason — that is an engine-side policy, not a client problem.
dataCheck.credentials: Session, access credential and refresh credential all received (length {{session}} / {{access}} / {{refresh}})
dataCheck.listUsersHint: Fetch the user list and show the email of the first few; each email can sign in once.
dataCheck.loginHint: "Sign in as this account" lets the browser remember the sign-in, so later protected calls carry it; "Get the sign-in credential only" returns the credential without storing it in the browser.
dataCheck.loginTestHint: These endpoints exist only on the development instance; a production engine does not register them and answers 404.
dataCheck.loginWebResult: Signed in as {{email}}: status {{status}} · valid for {{minutes}} min
dataCheck.noEmailForLogin: This account has no email; test sign-in accepts email only
dataCheck.scaffoldHint: The two public calls run for real. The protected pair can be pressed too, but sign-in is not wired yet, so failing is expected. Every request carries the current language and theme.
dataCheck.statesHint: The four stages of one fetch: not started, in progress, done, failed — shown with the public GET.
dataCheck.title: API check
